messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a quick, step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a good wipe‑down, polish the finish, and tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑maintained instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Shoot from multiple angles (body, neck, headstock, strings, any flaws). Use natural light and a neutral background. | Great photos attract buyers and reduce the chance of returns. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local classifieds. Note price ranges for similar models, ages, and conditions. | Helps you set a realistic, competitive price. | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | Include:
• Brand, model, year, and serial number
• Condition (new, like new, used, any damage)
• Features (pickup type, finish, custom work)
• Reason for selling
• Price (fixed or “best offer”)
• Shipping options (if applicable) | Transparency builds trust and speeds up the sale. | | **5. Choose Your Platforms** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments, global reach.
• **eBay** – auction or fixed price, large audience.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassle.
• **Local music stores** – consignment or direct purchase.
• **Reddit** (r/Guitar or r/AcousticGuitar) – niche community. | Different platforms reach different buyer types; use a mix for maximum exposure. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target price to allow room for negotiation. If you’re in a hurry, price a bit lower. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a buffer keeps you from underselling. | | **7. Handle Inquiries Promptly** | Respond within 24 hrs, answer questions honestly, and offer additional photos if requested. | Quick replies keep buyers engaged and reduce the risk of losing interest. | | **8. Arrange Safe Transactions** | • For local sales: meet in a public place (coffee shop, police station, or a store’s front desk).
• For online sales: use secure payment methods (PayPal, Venmo, or a bank transfer).
• Ship with insurance and tracking if you’re sending it. | Protects both parties and ensures you receive payment. | | **9. Finalize the Sale** | Provide a simple receipt or bill of sale that lists the guitar’s details, sale price, and both parties’ signatures. | Useful for record‑keeping and potential tax purposes. | | **10. Follow Up** | Ask the buyer for a quick review or feedback if you’re using a platform that allows it. | Positive reviews boost future sales and build your reputation. | ### Quick Tips & Common Pitfalls | Tip | Why It Helps | |-----|--------------| | **Showcase Unique Features** | If your guitar has a custom inlay, a special finish, or a high‑end pickup, highlight it. | | **Mention Any Repairs** | If you’ve had a neck reset or a new bridge installed, disclose it. Buyers appreciate honesty. | | **Avoid Over‑Pricing** | Even a great instrument can sit unsold if priced too high. | | **Be Prepared to Negotiate** | Most buyers will try to get a discount; decide in advance how low you’re willing to go. | | **Check Local Laws** | Some jurisdictions require a sales tax receipt or have specific rules for instrument sales. | | **Consider Trade‑In** | If you’re buying a new guitar, many stores offer trade‑in credits that can offset the cost. | ### Example Listing (Reverb) ``` Title: 2015 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition Description: - Brand: Yamaha - Model: FG800 - Year: 2015 - Finish: Natural - Condition: Like new – no scratches, no cracks, strings replaced last month. - Features: Solid spruce top, nato/okume back & sides, 25.5" scale, 12‑string pickup. - Reason for selling: Upgrading to a 12‑string. Price: $650 (Best Offer) Photos: 8 high‑resolution images (body, neck, headstock, strings, any minor blemishes). Shipping: Will ship via UPS Ground with insurance ($50). Local pickup available in Seattle. Contact: DM me on Reverb or email me at example@email.com. Payment via PayPal or Venmo. ``` Feel free to adapt the template to your own guitar’s specifics. Good luck with the sale! If you need help drafting a listing or choosing a platform, just let me know.
